extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in combinatorics/poset and lattice theory (readers of a combinatorics textbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Solutions and explanatory notes for exercises in a combinatorics/textbook chapter on posets, lattices, and related enumerative constructions. Contains definitions, bijections, counting formulae, recurrences, and references for each exercise result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence relation on Hasse-diagram edges and decomposition into saturated chains (Exercise 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define e,f in E (edges of the Hasse diagram of P) to be equivalent if e has vertices s,u and f has vertices t,u such that either both s<u and t<u or both s>u and t>u; extend by reflexivity/transitivity. Under the stated condition on P the equivalence classes are paths and cycles. Choosing a set of edges, no two consecutive, from each equivalence class yields a partition of P into disjoint saturated chains; elements not on a chosen edge form one-element saturated chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counting: number of ways to choose such an edge-set from a path of length ℓ is Fibonacci number F_{ℓ+2}; from a cycle of length ℓ is Lucas number L_ℓ (see Exercise 1.40). References: result due to R. Stanley, Amer. Math. Monthly 99 (1992).

rubrics_metrics.name: ai equals number of strict surjective order-preserving maps (Exercise 59)
rubrics_metrics.description: For given poset P and integer i, a_i is the number of strict surjective maps τ: P → [i] (i.e., τ is surjective and s < t in P implies τ(s) < τ(t)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This characterization can be proved by induction and is referenced to R. Stanley, Discrete Math. 4 (1973), 77–82.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijection between dropless labelings and acyclic orientations (sketch following Exercise 60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a dropless labeling f of P define orientation o(f) of inc(P) by orienting edge st as s→t iff f(s) < f(t). Then o is acyclic. Conversely, from any acyclic orientation o the unique minimal source s must be labeled 1 in any dropless labeling giving o; remove s and proceed inductively to construct a unique dropless labeling f with o = o(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a one-to-one correspondence between dropless labelings of P and acyclic orientations of inc(P); proof uses the source chain argument and induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijection from permutations to saturated chains via descent sets (Exercise 61)
rubrics_metrics.description: Map a permutation w to a chain of compositions σ_{D(w[1])} ⋖ σ_{D(w[2])} ⋖ ⋯ ⋖ σ_{D(w[n])} leading from 1 to σ = σ_{D(w[n])}; this establishes a bijection from S_n to saturated chains in the composition poset C, and the number of saturated chains from 1 to σ (where σ corresponds to descent set S) equals β_n(S) (the number of permutations with descent set S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, summing over all S yields total number of saturated chains = n!. See Björner–Stanley observation and Exercise 3.134 references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Gamma function for factorial extension when argument is half-integer (note after Exercise 65)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equation 3.116 continues to hold if 2t is an odd integer provided any factorial m! appearing is replaced by Γ(m+1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace factorials by Gamma values to extend identities to noninteger (half-integer) cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrences for W_n and generating-function identity (Exercise 66(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurrences: W_{2n} = W_{2n-1} + q^2 W_{2n-2}, and W_{2n+1} = q W_{2n} + W_{2n-1} (for n ≥ 1). From these one derives a closed-form generating function F(x) given in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive the generating function by multiplying the recurrences by appropriate powers of x (x^{2n} and x^{2n+1}) and summing over n; algebraic simplification produces F(x) as stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear extensions of Z_n correspond to alternating permutations; Euler numbers (Exercise 66(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence σ is a linear extension of Z_n iff the sequence n+σ(t_1),...,n+σ(t_n) is an alternating permutation of [n]; hence e(Z_n) equals the Euler number E_n and the exponential generating function Σ e(Z_n) x^n/n! = tan x + sec x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 1.6.1 and the standard bijection between alternating permutations and linear extensions of the zigzag poset Z_n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence for generating functions counting order-preserving maps G_m(x) (Exercise 66(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: By adjoining an extra element t_{n+1} to Z_n to create Z_{n+1} and partitioning blocks, one derives a recurrence relation among generating functions G_m(x) encoding numbers of order-preserving maps into chains of given size; initial conditions given by G_1(x)=1/(1-x) and G_2(x)=1/(1-x-x^2) (as stated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct order-preserving maps by decomposing into blocks and using combinatorial classes; see references to Stanley and Ziegler for details and corrected notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dilworth's theorem and its dual (Exercise 73 and related notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a finite poset P has width k then it can be partitioned into k chains (Dilworth's theorem). The dual statement (about antichains and chains intersection properties) follows more easily: an antichain intersects a chain in at most one element and dual arguments yield complementary statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original proof due to R. P. Dilworth (Proc. Symp. Appl. Math., 1960); applications and alternative proofs referenced (Greene–Kleitman, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Sperner property for Boolean lattice B_n (Exercise 78(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The lattice B_n has the strong Sperner property: a maximum-size union of k antichains is the union of the k largest ranks. Consequently, μ_i (the sizes of largest unions) equal the i-th largest binomial coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other posets with strong Sperner property include finite products of chains and certain distributive lattices; reference K. Engel, Sperner Theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjecture about comparable pair frequency in linear extensions (discussion in 70(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjectured that for any finite poset P there exist s,t in P such that f(s) < f(t) in at least 1/3 of the linear extensions of P; poset 2+1 shows this bound would be best possible if true; results of Brightwell–Felsner–Trotter give optimal bounds for a class of thin posets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an open conjecture (as of the references); consult Brightwell et al. for partial results and constructions achieving bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedekind-type counts for free distributive lattices FD(n) (Exercise 71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The enumeration result for FD(n) (free distributive lattice on n generators) is classical due to Dedekind; the same method gives FD(P) results for more general posets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the cited corollary and references (e.g., Jónsson) for proofs and related enumeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping-rule interpretation and recurrence for complete dual binary tree order-ideals (Exercise 74)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L_n = J(P_n) where P_n is the complete dual binary tree of height n. An order ideal I corresponds to a stopping rule for a coin-toss walk on the tree; this structure yields the functional equation F(L_n,q) = 1 + q F(L_{n-1},q)^2 (as indicated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the decomposition P_n = 1 ⊕ (1 + P_{n-1}) and analyze choices of order ideals to derive the recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lattice structure on graph orientations (Exercise 75)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of acyclic orientations (or certain orientations) of a graph can be endowed with a lattice structure; Propp gave a lattice-theoretic proof and alternative proofs using hyperplane arrangements exist (Ehrenborg & Slone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structural result links graph orientations to lattice theory and hyperplane arrangements; see the cited preprint and Order 26 (2009).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stembridge's 'q = 1 phenomenon' and cyclic sieving (discussion in 79)
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal definition: given an involution (or cyclic group) acting on a finite set S and a natural combinatorial/statistic polynomial f on S, the triple (S, action, f) exhibits a 'q = 1 phenomenon' (or more generally cyclic sieving) when evaluation of the polynomial at certain roots of unity counts fixed points of the action. Stembridge and later Reiner–Stanton–White developed these phenomena; many examples and generalizations are cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Stembridge J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 68 (1994) and the cyclic sieving paper by Reiner–Stanton–White (JCTA 2004) for formal definitions and worked examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion operator reverses parity of linear extension (Exercise 80(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The promotion operator ∂ on the set of linear extensions L(P) always reverses the parity (sign) of a linear extension f to which it is applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See R. Stanley, Advances in Appl. Math. 34 (2005), Corollary 2.2, for details and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign-imbalance and sign-balancedness results for posets (Exercise 82)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are computations and results (e.g., D. White) concerning the 'sign imbalance' (sum of ±1 over linear extensions weighted by sign) for rectangular posets p×q and conjectures/extensions for general finite order ideals of N^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See White, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 95 (2001) and Stanley for conjectures and computed examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of parity-reversing involution when no P-domino tableau exists (Exercise 83)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a P-domino tableau does not exist for poset P with |P| = 2m, then there is an explicit involution on the set of linear extensions E_P that reverses parity; this yields sign-balance consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the involution by transposing a certain pair a_{2i-1}, a_{2i} where they are incomparable; see Stanley's Corollary referenced for the parity-reversing involution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Möbius inversion identities relating f and g (Exercise 86)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given G(t) = Σ_{u ≥ t} g(u) one has μ(ˆ0,u)G(u) = Σ_{t ≥ ˆ0} g(t) and Möbius inversion yields g(s) = Σ_{t ≥ s} μ(s,t) G(t) and related identities (equations (3.140) and (3.141)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these standard inversion formulas to transform cumulative sums into pointwise values and vice versa; referenced result due to P. Doubilet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain-coefficient identity in incidence algebra expansions (Exercise 87)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a chain C = ˆ0 < t1 < ⋯ < tk < ˆ1, the coefficient of the product f(t1)⋯f(tk) on the left-hand side equals Σ_{C' ⊇ C} (−1)^{k+1} μ(ˆ0,t1) μ(t1,t2)⋯ μ(tk,ˆ1), summing over chains C' containing C (Proposition 3.8.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set f(t)=1 to obtain cancellation identities; apply boolean interval evaluations to simplify sums (see (c) and (d) parts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crapo complementation theorem (Exercise 92)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Crapo complementation theorem' provides criteria/identities for complements in lattices and related topological consequences; originally due to H. H. Crapo (J. Combin. Theory 1966).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For topological aspects see A. Björner, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 30 (1981).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant identities for incidence/ζ-matrices (Exercise 96(a),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M = [M(s,t)] with M(s,t) = ζ(s,t) f(s,t). Ordering rows/columns by a linear extension makes M triangular and det M = ∏_s f(s,s). More generally det[F(s∧t)] = det(M^T ζ) = det M, yielding Lindström/Wilf determinant results; special cases give combinatorial consequences (Dowling–Wilson applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use matrix factorizations with incidence (ζ) matrices and Möbius-function diagonal matrices to deduce nonvanishing determinants and combinatorial injectivity/permutation existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of complementing permutation in geometric lattices via matrix method (Exercise 97)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct matrices ζ, Δ_0 = diag(μ(ˆ0,t)), Δ_1 = diag(μ(t,ˆ1)). Then C = ζ Δ_1 ζ^T Δ_0 ζ has entries zero unless u and v are complements. If det C ≠ 0 (under hypotheses) a nonzero term in det C expansion yields a permutation mapping elements to complements; this proves existence of a 'complementing permutation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This elegant proof is due to R. M. Wilson; counterexamples where μ(ˆ0,t) = 0 for all t are exhibited (Figure 3.78).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of certain semimodular atomic lattices as Boolean lattices (Exercises 100–101)
rubrics_metrics.description: If L is atomic and semimodular and satisfies the given covering and join conditions (detailed in the solution), induction shows L ≅ B_n (the Boolean lattice). Proof uses properties of atoms, coatoms, and semimodularity to deduce structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed by induction on rank and analyze joins of atoms; standard lattice-theory arguments and references (e.g., G. Grätzer) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kung's matrix/Möbius-inversion injectivity result (Exercise 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the matrix [ζ(s,t)]_{s∈B,t∈A} has nonzero determinant then the restriction map f↦f|_A determines f on A by Möbius inversion; this implies existence of an injective rank-preserving map φ: B → L with specified properties (result due to J. P. S. Kung).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use induction on interval lengths and Möbius inversion to reconstruct values and deduce injectivity; see the cited Kung papers for applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion–contraction recurrence for number of acyclic orientations (Exercise 109(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a graph G and edge e = {u,v}, the number of acyclic orientations satisfies ao(G) = ao(G\e) + ao(G/e), with initial condition ao(G)=1 if G has no edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: classify orientations of G by whether u and v are oriented consistently or contracted; show exactly one of the two orientations obtained by reattaching u or v is acyclic except in the ao(G/e) cases. Reference: R. Stanley, Discrete Math. 5 (1973).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical arrangement intersection-lattice equals connected-partitions lattice and chromatic polynomial relations (Exercises 107–109)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intersection lattice L_{B_G} of the graphical arrangement B_G is isomorphic to the lattice of connected partitions of G ordered by refinement. The chromatic polynomial χ_G(n) can be interpreted in terms of maps constant on blocks of partitions and expressed via Möbius inversion on that lattice; contraction-deletion identities for χ_G(n) follow combinatorially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define hyperplanes H_e for edges e by x_i - x_j = 0; intersections correspond to equalities of coordinates across components of spanning subgraphs. Use Whitney's theorem and Möbius inversion to relate χ_G and the arrangement polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitney's theorem for arrangements (Exercise 112 fragment)
rubrics_metrics.description: By Whitney’s theorem (Proposition 3.11.3) certain polynomial identities relating arrangement characteristic polynomials and partition enumerators hold (the text contains the start of such an identity: A(x) = ...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Proposition 3.11.3 and the surrounding section in the textbook for the complete statements and derivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinatorial identity and Kalai's topological theorem relating f- and g-vectors (Exercise 107 and discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under acyclicity/link vanishing hypotheses on a simplicial complex Δ (or an order ideal I of B_n) one can express the f-polynomial as (1+x)^{k+1} times a polynomial with nonnegative integer coefficients: Σ f_i x^i = (1+x)^{k+1} Σ g_i x^i (equation (3.142)). This is a combinatorial analogue of Kalai's deeper topological result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses require links of faces up to dimension k-1 to be acyclic; references: G. Kalai (Computational Commutative Algebra and Combinatorics), Stanley conjectures and Duval generalizations.
